Title: CRISPR gene editing
Content: "In 2012, the research team led by professor Jennifer Doudna and professor Emmanuelle Charpentier was the first group to file a patent application for the CRISPR-Cas9 system," which "could be programmed with RNA to edit genomic DNA." "In October 2020, researchers Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna were awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their work in this field." (The seminal paper: Jinek, Chylinski, Fonfara, Hauer, Doudna, Charpentier, Science 337:816-821, 28 June 2012.)

Title: Cas9
Content: "DNA cleavage requires the presence of a protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) located at the non-target strand." Cas9 is directed by "a guide RNA composed of two distinct RNA molecules: CRISPR RNA (crRNA) and trans-activating crRNA (tracrRNA)."
